jamal: FYI support is getting p99 complaints after we rolled runtime/v2.3.1 to canary. noticed tail creeping up ~00:10 after deployment. p50/p95 fine, p99 jumped from ~300ms to ~1.9s for /v1/generate in us-west. canary was 5% traffic across 12 pods.

lina: any 5xxs or client errors?

jamal: no 5xxs. errors = 0 but interactive UIs are stuttering. customers escalated.

mike: which changes were in v2.3.1? I saw dynamic-batching heuristics + fused-attn v3 in that roll. commit a1b2c3d.

anya: adding sre-bot for deploy telemetry.

sre-bot: Deploy: runtime/v2.3.1 -> canary (12 pods). Canary health: passing. Alert: p99_text_gen_us-west > baseline threshold at +00:11. Autoscaler: no events.

lina: pulled traces from the canary pool. here's a short summary: ```
route: /v1/generate (text)
seq_len: 256, 512 samples
kernel_path: fused_attn_v3 selected for many traces
batch_wait_ms configured: 15ms (dynamic-batching)
observed queue depth: spikes 20-30
exec latency median: 30ms
exec latency p99: 820ms - 1.2s
end-to-end p99: ~1.9s
```

mike: that smells like two-way interaction: fused kernel slower on some configs + dynamic batching increasing batch windows at low qps. fused_attn_v3 might be optimized for long seqs but regresses on 256/512 on our A100 driver.

jamal: can we reduce user-facing impact fast? opsbot can we reduce canary weight to 0% while we debug?

opsbot: Route change request: set runtime-canary weight -> 0%. Confirm to proceed.

lina: confirmed.

opsbot: Route updated. Canary weight is now 0%. Observed p99 on prod routes drop back to baseline within ~40s.

anya: mitigation successful. next: reproduce and bisect. mike can you run a targeted bisect between base and a1b2c3d focusing on dynamic-batching defaults and fused_attn_v3 heuristics?

mike: starting bisect plan: 1) microbench fused kernels seq=128/256/512/1024; 2) simulate low-qps canary with dynamic-batching enabled to observe queueing tail; 3) toggle batch_wait_ms. Immediate quick fix options: pin kernel-selector to legacy or reduce batch_wait_ms to 2-4ms.

lina: quick repro I ran locally: with batch_wait_ms>=12 and fused_attn_v3, p99 exec jumped significantly at low qps. gist of steps: ```
1) launch runtime image locally
2) set kernel-selector=fused_attn_v3
3) set batch_wait_ms=15
4) run seq_len=256 workload concurrency=18 throughput=low (~10 qps)
5) observe p99 tail and queue pileup
```

mike: thanks. that matches my intuition. fused_attn_v3 reduces compute for very long sequences but has more setup overhead on our current kernel and driver, so at typical 256/512 it loses in p99. Selector should have been gated by microbench p50+p99 across seq lengths.

anya: opened ticket INFRA-1215 to track root cause, bisect results, and add safety. also INC-2027 for the customer incident. severity P2.

mike: bisect initial findings: culprit commits: (1) enable fused_attn_v3 by default for "auto" selector; (2) increase default batch_wait_ms from 8 -> 15. Either alone can be okay, together they amplify tail under low qps. Reverting enablement of fused_attn_v3 removes the tail in microbench.

lina: recorded repro steps and artifacts in INFRA-1215: perf traces, flamegraphs, and the kernel microbench results.

jamal: customer line update: we reduced canary weight to 0% and are investigating. will follow up with a root cause and timeline.

mike: proposed immediate code mitigations: 1) change kernel selector to require both median and p99 perf improvement on microbench across a few seq lengths before flipping; 2) make dynamic-batching defaults conservative for canary pools (batch_wait_ms <= 4ms); 3) add an emergency circuit: if canary p99 > 2x baseline in a sliding 5-10 minute window, auto-pin selector=legacy and set batch_wait_ms=2.

anya: adding automated fallback as an action item. also adding a deployment checklist item: run microbench on target GPU/driver combos for seq lengths 128/256/512/1024 before enabling new kernel paths.

lina: will add microbench step to the canary runbook. also adding monitoring rule: alert when p99 delta > 1.5x baseline for a route within 10 minutes.

mike: opening PR for selector guard + fallback and testcases. tagging the PR with INFRA-1215.

opsbot: Incident logged: INC-2027. Assigned: mike, lina, anya. Slack thread will be linked to the incident.

jamal: thanks everyone. leaving this thread for follow-up in INFRA-1215/INC-2027. I'll coordinate customer comms. :thumbsup:
